issue_context.title: Recent changes in struct clusterMsg break cluster rolling upgrades
issue_context.body:
@madolson the math doesn't look right.  notused1 should be 30 bytes long as opposed to 16 because uint16_t is 2 bytes (16 bits). This will break cluster rolling upgrades.

_Originally posted by @PingXie in https://github.com/redis/redis/pull/9530#discussion_r794994327_

review_comments: Isn't this macro affected by -std=c99 so these asserts will never be checked?
@zuiderkwast It is affected, but why would they never be checked? We use `-std=c11` to get C11 atomics on relevant platforms, we just don't adopt C11 all over (yet).
OK, I though we use c99 everyehere. If we use c11 in at least one build, we'll catch it. :dart:
I can add an implementation for static_assert for pre-C11 to make this behavior consistent across all supported compilers.  thoughts?
@PingXie I don't think it is necessary, since as long as we have at least one C11 compiler in CI (and we do), we're covered.

Sure. It is actually pretty trivial (3 lines) but yeah agreed that there is no urgency. 

```
#ifndef static_assert
#define static_assert(expr, lit) extern char __static_assert_failure[(expr) ? 1:-1]
#endif
```
PS, to your earlier question, the string literal is no longer required in [C23](https://en.cppreference.com/w/c/language/_Static_assert) but still needed for C11, which is what I meant by "old compliers", relatively speaking :).
